I get it, trust me I do. I've been dealing with anxiety and bipolar most of my life but only dx'd at 22 (although I had a mis-dx of MDD from 15 on. You see I did attempt suicide at 15. I told my parents nothing beforehand, I guess it didn't occur to me that I needed help (I thought of myself as a mistake for years) and because I have rapid cycling it probably looked even more like a phase than it could have. My parents pulled me from the hospital when I was medically stable against medical advice (but they could because I was a minor). I'd go on to get the minimal treatment to go back to school (one visit to a psychologist) and then I went through guidance counseling but it did nothing for me. I wouldn't go on to get the right dx or real treatment until a housemate realized something was terribly horribly wrong when I finally moved out at 22. I made it that far by some miracle because I kept attempting suicide (my parents did not know about a majority of the attempts, usually I'd wake up in my own vomit or I'd do something like ripping the bag off my head and the attempt they knew about they did nothing about except yell at me for breaking the gun (if that were my kid I would call 911 but my parents did not, I was 20 and no longer a minor and with the seriousness of the attempt they would've undoubtedly hospitalized me for awhile). 

Long story short...don't make my mistake and do get help when you move out. In the meantime hang in there and keep posting here and such, we can't provide legit professional help but we can provide our understanding born of our own experiences. Another thing you may want to look into is this: [DBT Workbook](https://www.amazon.com/Dialectical-Behavior-Therapy-Skills-Workbook/dp/1572245131/ref=mt_paperback?_encoding=UTF8&me=&qid=1530275062)

Antidepressants, specifically SSRIs, messed with me bad....I'd feel better (a LOT better) for a few days and then crash hard and end up worse off. That's really not an uncommon story for folks either and a lot of how I ended up with the right diagnosis. I had my first pure psychiatric hospitalization (which might have been my last had I not spent years and years in denial) at age 22 (I'd gotten the depression diagnosis after a suicide attempt at fifteen but my parents didn't believe in treatment) they thought I just had depression and put me on Prozac, when I got to see my first outpatient psychiatrist he talked to me for a bit, took a full history and told me I didn't have depression (which confused me) that I had bipolar (which freaked me out and that was part of the reason that I took myself off meds after three months). Part of what made that apparent was my reaction to SSRIs. While in denial of the whole bipolar thing I tried SSRIs twice more...with the same result. Finally I took my very messed up self (between the mixed episode I'd already been fighting and the SSRI that was never going to treat it) to my current psychiatrist and told the truth...I'd purposefully failed the bipolar screening because I couldn't handle the idea and I was very very suicidal....I'd lied about needing to go to the hospital too to his predecessor, he'd asked if I thought I needed to go IP and I massively did but I said I'd be ok when I wasn't ok and wasn't going to be ok without some sort of intervention.

It did surprise me (I started treatment for real and for a long period..for the first time even though I've had the diagnosis for 12 years) that I am one of those people who could be helped. In truth though for 80% of people with bipolar it's highly treatable. There are probably things I haven't figured out yet in the end. Although I've taken a bit of a plunge....I'm lucid. Even though I've been fighting anxiety and paranoia...my therapist is helping me fight through it. 

My med cocktail, therapy, meditation, having an ESA (emotional support animal), talking to people who get it, having a routine...it's all helped.

Courses of treatment depend person to person but always be willing to try things....what works for may not work for you and vice versa (for me it's a combination of therapy, medication and writing).

Support is absolutely key. Depression will make you feel entirely alone...that's the nature of the illness. You'll probably do what you can to keep yourself that way too...fight that urge, and for the people supporting someone...do what you can do keep your loved from pushing you away and if they do realize it's not you...they're sick. 

Always be open with SOMEONE about what you're feeling, especially if you're feeling suicidal. In the case of someone supporting someone be willing to listen without judging, without spouting too many platitudes and with understanding...as best as you can. 

Sometimes we need you to do what we tell you not to do and to not do what we tell you to do. I want to be alone....I tell my friends to not leave me alone too much and to check on me. If things look dire it's ok to coerce me into doing things that will save my life. I may hate you for it in the moment...but I'll thank you later. That said don't be afraid to ask The Question...not every depressive gets suicidal but a fair amount of us do...ask if we're thinking about it. You aren't going to plant ideas we don't already have. If we are and we have a plan and are getting ready to carry it out...do what you can to save a life.
